svg.title: Reports & month-end — A noticeable difference in 1 of 4 tests
svg.desc: Reports & month-end: A noticeable difference in 1 of 4 tests. Median per test for SQL Server, MySQL and PostgreSQL, each on its own scale from zero; coloured bars mark differences a user would notice, grey bars ties and differences too small to notice. Sales by customer and month: No noticeable difference. MySQL is 4.61× slower, but that is only 53.1 ms more per yearly report (noticeable from 1 s and 10%). Trial balance: No noticeable difference. SQL Server is 7.44× slower, but that is only 226 ms more per period (noticeable from 1 s and 10%). GL account details for a year: No noticeable difference. SQL Server is 4.28× slower, but that is only 20.5 ms more per account (noticeable from 1 s and 10%). Deep paging and counting in a 300,000-line journal: MySQL noticeably slower than both. 19.9 s more per pass of 12 requests (70% slower). SQL Server and PostgreSQL tie.
